mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates economic expansion, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher during GDP growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity prices.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 5% in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >50% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS in a tightening cycle increases borrowing costs, reducing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in a month
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased construction and economic activity, boosting S&P 500.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur when housing starts rise.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production signals increased economic output, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher during production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equities.
GDP growth combined with rising consumer spending indicates strong demand, boosting S&P 500.
failure_condition: Returns are not higher when both proxies increase.
